three_beat_engine.title: Three-Beat Pedagogical Engine
three_beat_engine.definition: A narrative learning structure (Goal → Complication → Pivot) ensuring technical vocabulary attaches directly to human decisions and real frictions rather than passive memorization.
three_beat_engine.context: The habit is the complication; the replacement decision is the pivot. Terms must land on friction points.

falsifiable_hypothesis.title: Falsifiable Hypothesis
falsifiable_hypothesis.definition: A precise, testable proposition specifying observable telemetry conditions that would prove an assumption false before investigation or execution begins.
falsifiable_hypothesis.context: If you cannot name what disproves you before running queries, you are sightseeing rather than diagnosing.

prediction_gate.title: Prediction Gate
prediction_gate.definition: An interactive checkpoint requiring learners to commit to an observable outcome in writing before revealing telemetry or solution data.
prediction_gate.context: Combats the hindsight bias where observed outcomes feel retroactively obvious.

bridge_card.title: Curriculum Bridge Card
bridge_card.definition: A visual and conceptual handoff component placed at the end of a narrative chapter that directs the learner to its companion workbench exercise.
bridge_card.context: Connects conceptual tension in the story directly to hands-on muscle memory in the workbench.

telemetry_stream.title: Telemetry Stream
telemetry_stream.definition: A continuous, high-volume flow of timestamped diagnostic records, event logs, or metric samples emitted by operational systems.
telemetry_stream.context: Raw telemetry requires normalization and structured scoping to prevent cognitive overload.

baseline_drift.title: Baseline Drift
baseline_drift.definition: The gradual divergence of system metrics from historical norms caused by changing workloads, configuration drift, or stealthy adversary activity.
baseline_drift.context: Distinguishing seasonal organic drift from malicious degradation requires comparative peer clustering.

cardinality.title: Cardinality
cardinality.definition: The uniqueness of data values contained in a particular column or field, such as unique IP addresses, session IDs, or transaction tags.
cardinality.context: High cardinality fields can overwhelm indexers but provide critical forensic discrimination.

circuit_breaker.title: Circuit Breaker Pattern
circuit_breaker.definition: A defensive design pattern that automatically halts outbound calls to a failing remote dependency once an error threshold is crossed, allowing recovery.
circuit_breaker.context: Prevents catastrophic cascading failures across microservices during network partition events.

backpressure.title: Backpressure
backpressure.definition: A flow-control signaling mechanism where downstream consumers signal upstream producers to throttle ingestion rate when queues reach capacity.
backpressure.context: Without backpressure, buffering systems exhaust memory and drop packets under burst traffic.

graceful_degradation.title: Graceful Degradation
graceful_degradation.definition: The ability of a system to maintain essential core functions when peripheral subsystems or downstream dependencies fail.
graceful_degradation.context: Ensures critical operations continue with cached data or simplified interfaces during outages.

least_frequency_analysis.title: Least-Frequency Analysis (Long Tail)
least_frequency_analysis.definition: A statistical investigation technique that aggregates events by occurrence count and sorts from least frequent to most frequent to expose rare outliers.
least_frequency_analysis.context: Adversary implants often hide in the single 1-of-a-million connection rather than top-volume lists.

synthetic_benchmark.title: Synthetic Benchmark
synthetic_benchmark.definition: An artificially generated operational test workload used to measure reproducible system performance under controlled stress conditions.
synthetic_benchmark.context: Guarantees deterministic comparative analysis without risking production system instability.
